OmaStats 1.4 puts real readouts on vertical bars, adds an optional VRAM readout, and picks up ZFS pools.

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

![OmaStats on a vertical bar in dark and light themes: CPU, two GPUs with VRAM, memory, disks, network and sensors](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.4.0/omastats-1.4.0-vertical-bar.png)

## New

- **Vertical bars show data.** Before, a vertical bar only showed each module's letters stacked on top of each other. Now each readout puts its label across the bar, with the graph or ring and the figure under it. It follows the look you picked for that module. Network and disk speeds show one rate per line, colored like their half of the graph. Figures shrink to fit the bar instead of being cut off.
- **VRAM readout.** Settings → Bar → GPU → "Show VRAM in bar" adds a `VRM` readout next to each selected GPU that reports memory use, in the same look as that GPU's readout. The GPU tab now shows load and VRAM history graphs side by side, and with utilization colors on, both use the same four grades as the bar. By @jsonMartin (#13).
- **ZFS pools.** A mounted ZFS pool shows up as one volume on the Disks page and in the disk readouts, at its shortest mount path. Its space comes from `zfs list`, so snapshots count as used. Its drive is the first data drive listed by `zpool list`. Both tools run only when a ZFS dataset is mounted. By @dieuwedeboer (#15).

## Known limitations

- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks, which take the least space.

## Thanks
